Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 About the team 
 Stripe Checkout helps any business–from fast-growing startups to enterprises–accept payments without building their checkout from scratch. We have a suite of checkout surfaces that range from no- and low-code checkout pages to embedded payment forms and highly customized checkout flows. We’re expanding the suite to support emerging business models and continually optimizing so we can ensure Stripe has the most profitable, safest checkouts on the internet.

 What you’ll do 
 As a Staff Designer on Checkout, you'll lead the visual and interaction design direction for our most opinionated and optimized checkout surfaces. You’ll define how checkouts should flex to support emerging business models and underserved verticals, taking complex merchant needs and translating them to simple, conversion-optimized solutions. You’ll also contribute to and evolve the backing design system for our checkout surfaces.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Define the design direction for new features and checkout surfaces across the conversion funnel 

• Lead design explorations from initial concept through launch 

• Evolve and push boundaries on visual language, component patterns, and design systems 

• Shape early product strategy through design exploration and rapid prototyping, making abstract opportunities tangible for product and engineering partners 

• Represent Checkout in senior reviews and establish the creative bar for new product directions 
 
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 8+ years of relevant experience at a tech, product-driven company 

• Deep fluency in visual design, interaction design, systems thinking, and prototyping with AI tools 

• Experience leading complex work in close partnership with product management engineering, and design leadership 

• Experience shaping ambiguous spaces and driving clarity through design 

• Confident presenting work to senior leaders and skilled at communicating design decisions through clear, compelling storytelling 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience leading changes to a design system 

• Skilled in explaining your work, process, and decisions to cross-functional stakeholders and crave feedback to help you produce your best work 

• Background in SaaS, e-commerce, or fintech products

 About Stripe

 About the team 
 Stripe’s Design organization builds the product and brand experiences that millions of businesses and developers rely on. We’re a cross-functional, global organization of product designers, content designers, design researchers, design systems engineers, motion designers, and design program specialists.

 Our mission is to make economic infrastructure simple and accessible. Design plays a central role by making complex flows understandable, crafting clear product language, and building consistent systems that scale.

 The Design Operations team leads Design’s business operations, runs cross-organizational programs, and builds the systems that help teams collaborate and produce high-quality work. Design Program Managers guide complex programs through the design lifecycle and apply design thinking to our operating model. They prototype and iterate on how our team works.

 We’re looking for a Design Program Manager to partner with the Research team. This full-time role reports to the Head of Design Operations.

 What you’ll do 
 Responsibilities 
 

• Lead and build programs for the Research organization. Develop and implement processes and resources that support impactful research and scale the use of user insights across Stripe. 

• Improve our operating model and processes, including automating tasks, improving workflows, and developing repeatable methodologies. Measure the impact of these changes. 

• Prepare researchers to use agentic workflows, including designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows. 

• Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills for Research workflows and responsibilities. 

• Evaluate and implement new tools with researchers and cross-functional partners to support new capabilities across Stripe. 

• Work with researchers and designers across disciplines, skills, backgrounds, and specialties. Identify patterns and scale successful tools and approaches for broader team use. 

• Partner with Research leadership and the Design Operations team to balance competing priorities and make effective use of team resources. Identify potential obstacles and risks to key programs. Develop solutions, solve problems effectively, and use decision-making frameworks to support timely resolution. 

• Source and evaluate third-party vendors when needed. Work with Legal, Security, and Procurement to onboard and pay vendors, including managing statements of work, business terms, and budgets. 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

 

• You understand research work. You have direct experience in Design or can quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures relevant to Stripe researchers. You recognize that understanding someone’s work is necessary before changing it. 

• You have hands-on experience building artificial intelligence (AI) agents, automations, and tools. You’ve built solutions that changed how work gets done, and you can build alongside the people you support. 

• You’re an effective coach and communicator. You adapt your approach to different audiences and help people adopt new ways of working. 

• You recognize patterns and think in systems. When you build something that works for one person, you look for ways to make it useful to others. 

• You’re persistent and versatile, with skills that can apply across the company. 

• You prioritize action and speed. You can show someone a useful proof of concept on their own deliverable today, while continuing to build toward longer-term platform goals. 
 
 Minimum requirements 
 

• 5+ years of experience in design thinking, qualitative or quantitative research, user experience, or program management, including experience partnering with research teams. 

• Demonstrated hands-on experience building AI-powered tools, agents, automations, or workflows that improved real work processes for designers, researchers, creative teams, or product teams. 

• Experience coaching, teaching, or enabling others, formally or informally, with evidence of changes in how people work. 

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners. 

• Experience working across multiple workstreams and relationships at the same time. You’ll support a Research team that works across Stripe’s product, marketing, support, and design teams. 

• A product-builder mindset for solving the last-mile problem: turning standalone AI experiments into polished, production-ready products that are easy to find and use. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience with research and design tooling ecosystems, such as Qualtrics, Sprig, Figma, Dovetail, or design system management tools. 

• Experience with AI development tools and platforms, such as Claude, Claude Code, Codex, custom agent frameworks, application programming interface (API) integrations, or workflow automation tools. 

• Experience with change management, organizational transformation, or large-scale enablement programs. 

• Experience building and scaling internal tools, templates, or playbooks adopted beyond your immediate team.

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI.  We’re looking for a Brand Designer to join the Figma Brand Studio and focus on designing for the web. This role will help up-level some of our most important surfaces—our marketing websites—in brand-forward, novel, and unexpected ways.

 This role sits at the intersection of web design, software storytelling, and brand. You’ll need expert visual and UX instincts, a deep curiosity about our products, and a point of view on how to make product stories land on the web—showing what Figma can do, not just telling. You’re someone who loves to tinker and experiment. You have a deep understanding of accessibility, and you’re comfortable taking ideas from early sketch to working prototype, partnering with web engineers to bring new patterns and interactions to life. Working closely across Brand and Marketing, you’ll shape everything from site structure and navigation to launch, campaign, and event experiences. You’ll also help evolve the web design system that helps the team ship quality work at speed. You’ll play a central role in defining how Figma shows up on the web through experiences that are inventive, accessible, and beautifully crafted.

 This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

 What you’ll do at Figma: 
 

• Own and drive best-in-class UX and visual design across Figma’s marketing websites, from concept through prototype and production 

• Tell Figma’s software story on the web in compelling, inventive ways, working with Product Marketing and Content Strategy to show (not just tell) what our products can do 

• Prototype and develop new web patterns and interactions that move past standard SaaS conventions, and partner with web engineers to make them real 

• Design brand-forward web experiences for launches, campaigns, and events that feel novel and unexpected, while staying accessible and performant 

• Shape site structure, information architecture, and navigation to better bring our content strategy to life and serve customers’ needs 

• Evolve and contribute to our web design system, including templates and components that help the team ship quality work at speed 

• Share learnings, experiments, and techniques with Brand Studio and partners to raise the bar across the org 
 
 
 We'd love to hear from you if you have: 
 

• 5+ years designing websites, with a portfolio that shows creative range, strong visual, interaction, and typographic craft, and a clear point of view on telling software stories on the web 

• Fluent in designing, prototyping, and building with Figma, and curious about new design, build, and AI tools, with clear opinions on how and when to use them 

• Strong systems thinking, grounded in information architecture, UX and accessibility best practices, and experience contributing to and evolving design systems and templates 

• Experience using research and data to run experiments and drive decisions 

• Comfortable with ambiguity and able to drive concepts from start to finish on your own, partnering closely with design, copy, strategy, engineering, product marketing, and growth along the way

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses.  The Product Design team is made up of several groups that define, create, and deliver all user-facing aspects of Stripe's products. jobs.description:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the role 
 Growth at Anthropic is about helping people discover what Claude can do and make it part of how they work, from someone's first session to an entire company rolling out Claude. We're a small design team working across all of Anthropic's products, on problems that often don't have established playbooks, because the products and the capabilities behind them change so quickly.

 We drive growth by making the product itself better, favoring foundational changes and new product experiences over small optimizations. Our focus spans whatever most limits Anthropic's growth, and priorities can shift quickly.

 As a senior Product Designer on Growth, you'll own how Claude grows with people who use it for their everyday work. You'll dig into why some people make Claude a habit and others don't, find the real bottlenecks, and lead the product changes that move them. You'll set the vision for this area, partner closely with product, engineering, and data science, and raise the quality bar for the designers around you.

 We're looking for designers who thrive in ambiguity and pair sharp diagnostic judgment with exceptional craft. You form a clear point of view from messy signals, prototype quickly to test it, and drive alignment across teams to ship it. You use tools like Claude Code to explore ideas and push what's possible.

 Key responsibilities 
 

• Own growth for how people use Claude in their everyday work, end to end, as your full-time focus 

• Diagnose what drives deep, habitual use and what blocks it, combining data, research, and hands-on time in the product 

• Set an opinionated vision for the area and turn it into a roadmap with your PM, engineering, and data science partners 

• Redesign core parts of the product to drive growth, from onboarding and first-run experiences to the everyday workflows people rely on most 

• Shape hypotheses and experiments, and judge results with a nuanced view of how we win, not just the topline metric 

• Deliver exceptionally crafted interactions and set the quality bar for your area 

• Drive alignment with partner teams whose work touches your area, connecting individual use to team and company adoption 

• Mentor other designers, and frame problems clearly enough that others can own them 

• Prototype and test ideas quickly with Claude Code and other AI tools 
 
 Minimum qualifications 
 

• A portfolio of shipped product design work that shows product vision and a high level of craft 

• Experience owning growth for a major product area end to end, including diagnosing problems and setting direction 

• Deep growth design experience in activation, onboarding, retention, engagement, or expansion, on a product at meaningful scale 

• Hands-on experience designing, launching, and interpreting experiments, and using them to make product decisions 

• Fluency with product analytics such as funnels, retention, and engagement 

• Proficiency with design, prototyping, and AI tools, such as Figma and Claude Code, and a habit of learning new tools to push what's possible 

• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience driving alignment across product, engineering, and data science 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience leading growth strategy across multiple teams or product areas 

• Experience designing enterprise/B2B SaaS, productivity, or collaboration tools 

• Experience with product-led growth, from a single user to a team to a company-wide rollout 

• Experience mentoring designers or shaping a design practice 

• Comfort querying data yourself with SQL or a similar tool 

• Experience prototyping with front-end code (e.g., HTML/CSS/JS) 

• Experience defining AI-powered workflows for yourself or your team 

• A clear point of view on when a product should ask for attention, and when it should stay out of the way 

• Passion for building safe, beneficial AI that helps people do their best work 
 
 Representative projects 
 

• Diagnose why some people make a product part of their daily work and others drift away, then lead the changes that close the gap 

• Redesign a core part of the product so people return to it more often and get more value each time 

• Set the vision for a product's first-run experience and lead it through experiments to a redesigned, permanent flow 

• Design the path from one person's daily use to their whole team adopting it 
 The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

 For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

 Annual Salary: $305,000 — $460,000 USD Logistics 
 Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

 Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

 Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

 Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

 How we're different 
 We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

 The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

 Come work with us! 
 Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.description:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 About the team 
 Brand Studio lays the foundations that help Stripe accelerate. We do this by creating, evolving, and maintaining Stripe’s high-quality, versatile, and forward-looking brand design systems, experiences, and advertising campaigns. We sweat the details. We make it seem effortless.

 What you’ll do 
 This is an individual contributor role embedded directly within the Link brand team. You'll be the sole producer for Link, owning the full scope of creative operations end-to-end.

 You will be responsible for leading creative operations and creative production across our consumer brand Link, in close partnership with the Link Creative Director. This role is a hybrid mix of program management, project management, and creative production depending on the project phase. During certain periods you'll be focused on the 10,000 foot view of the program, and at other times you'll be working side-by-side with the creative team overseeing execution of every design detail during production.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Lead all Link brand program management, including roadmap development, budget oversight, and project scoping, timelines, and resourcing 

• Manage a high volume of simultaneous projects, ranging from small to large scale, and across surfaces — creative strategy, web, digital, social, brand systems, integrated campaigns, and email 

• Scale and evolve Link brand design systems in partnership with the Link Creative Director; continuously refine processes to keep pace with the work and reduce friction for the team 

• Partner closely with the XFN Design teams to ensure smooth execution, alignment and integration of design systems across all surfaces 

• Drive clarity and alignment with leadership, creatives, XFN partners, and external agencies 

• Own project management through documentation, tooling, trackers, standing meetings, org-wide updates, and Slack 

• Source, onboard, and oversee external creative agencies 

• Connect silos, socialize changes, anticipate risks, and provide actionable solutions for escalation to Brand Studio leadership 

• Handle challenges and blockers with ease; proactive in finding solutions, and always looking ahead for the team 

• Uphold and advocate for design quality with cross-functional teams and vendors 

• Inspire and sustain a culture of excellence by collaborating with creatives in best practices and processes 
 
 Who you are 
 Brand producers at Stripe are operators first. They find the work in the process — the right framework, the workback schedule that actually holds, the system that scales without breaking — and they measure success by how well the creative team around them can do their best work. They have strong design sense and bring it to bear on the operational decisions that protect quality and keep programs moving.

 The ideal candidate excels at keeping the work on track while maintaining (and raising) the bar on craft. They offer options and tradeoffs, crisply articulate decisions, iterate quickly, and collaborate with senior leadership, marketers, creatives, and agency partners. Most importantly, they are meticulous when it comes to details.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 6+ years of experience in similar roles and industries 

• Think users first — understand their needs, find interesting and unique solutions, and strive to consistently optimize how to best engage with them 

• Have a strong strategic acumen for developing complex program roadmaps and cross-functional processes in a fast-paced environment 

• Can manage the operational business of the team — budgets, resourcing, and program rhythm — while maintaining a clear point of view on where the program is headed and what it needs to get there 

• Can demonstrate strong design sense and deep production experience across multiple asset types: brand systems, web and digital surfaces, motion and animation, email templates, standardized reusable assets, and integrated campaigns 

• Actively use AI tooling in your day-to-day production work — for scheduling, workflow management, asset scaling, and operational efficiency — and have experience building or implementing AI systems that others on your team can adopt 

• Have experience operating in an in-house brand environment, not just agency or consultancy contexts, and understand the constraints that come with it: no dedicated bench, shared XFN resources, and direct accountability to a single creative leader rather than a client relationship 

• Proven excellence in producing creative systems that are optimized for scale and growth 

• Highly detail oriented and excel at simplifying complexity 

• Strong track record successfully influencing outcomes both internally and with agency partners 

• Can balance optimizing for speed and quality, with high craft and quality creative work 

• Are persuasive in explaining your work, process, and decisions 

• Excellent organization and presentation skills, and excel in written and verbal communication 

• Are passionate about Stripe's mission

 About the team 
 Public Goods at Stripe is focused on catalyzing products or services that would improve the world but don’t exist because the commercial motivations aren’t yet sufficient. By characterizing these goods, and altering the incentives, we hope to bring them to market faster. Our two main initiatives— Frontier , a $1.8B advanced market commitment to accelerate carbon removal, and Intercept , an effort to accelerate the elimination of respiratory infections—are partnerships between Stripe and some of the world’s most ambitious organisations, including Google, Anthropic, the OpenAI Foundation, and J.P. Morgan.

 What you’ll do 
 Stripe is looking for an entrepreneurial netizen to lead communications for our Public Goods programs. The success of Frontier and Intercept will be contingent on building strong networks of support and cooperation in the communities where they operate (researchers, scientists, technologists, healthcare). We’ll need to persuade people and organisations to change course: labs changing their research paths; entrepreneurs quitting their jobs to start something new; funders reprioritising their grant programs. You’ll laser in on the influential voices, and build targeted strategies to shift opinions and behaviours using traditional media, podcasts, video, substackers, influencers, events, and Twitter. You’ll craft compelling messaging on world-altering technologies; announce billions of dollars worth of grants and investments; publish opinionated editorial designed to inflect research fields; build communities of superfans; and manage coalitions of the world’s biggest companies and philanthropic organizations. If we’re successful, you’ll be instrumental in reducing CO2 in the atmosphere, ending respiratory infections, and whatever else comes next.

 Responsibilities 
 

• ‘Full stack’ comms leadership for Intercept and Frontier, from strategy and narrative development right through to having great stories and content out in the world. 

• Crafting the Intercept narrative (largely from scratch, it’s very early!), and evolving the Frontier story for the next phase. 

• Designing novel communications strategies from first principles to get journalists, influencers, policymakers, and substackers excited about these programs. 

• Writing excellent communications (i.e. announcements, social media posts, or opinion pieces). Note: we are unusually obsessive about the quality of our writing! 

• Partner with experts and leaders in the Frontier and Intercept teams: soliciting their ideas and expertise to inform the strategy, preparing them for media or podcast appearances, and building their profiles among important audiences. 

• Build excellent relationships with our partners (both funders and portfolio companies and projects) in pursuit of carefully orchestrated communications across many stakeholders 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

 Minimum requirements 
 

• Comfort with highly complex and technical subject matter; you don’t need to be a scientist yourself, but you will need to keep up with some very fast-moving ones on the team. 

• A superlative writer with a proven ability to translate complex, dense, technical information into compelling communications but which maximise fidelity. 

• High agency and autonomy: identifying gaps or risks, seeking out the context, and bringing fully formed ideas for leadership approval. 

• Experience in or around online movements which prize first-principles thinking, entrepreneurialism, and speed, like Silicon Valley, Progress, or Effective Altruism. 

• A strong intuition for how and why ideas spread, particularly on the internet. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience working with traditional media outlets is good, but not required.

 As a Designer on the Presence team, you'll own design across two distinct and high-visibility surface areas—Link (the Stripe one-click checkout experience and link.com) and Bridge (bridge.xyz—the Stripe stablecoin financial infrastructure, operating as its own standalone web property). These are some of the most strategically varied and creatively demanding surfaces in our portfolio—each with its own audience, brand voice, and design challenge.

 You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy—driving work from brief to launch, navigating ambiguity with confidence, and setting the quality bar for your focus areas. You'll shape the design systems and storytelling frameworks that make these surfaces scale, and you'll build deep expertise that makes you a go-to partner for the cross-functional teams you work alongside. This is a high-ownership role for a designer who is equally at home leading a complex project and sweating the details of a single layout.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Own the end-to-end design of your focus areas, Link and Bridge, from early strategy through final delivery, with minimal oversight 

• Drive clarity in ambiguous or loosely defined briefs by synthesizing user needs, business goals, and technical constraints into a coherent point of view 

• Lead cross-functional collaboration with engineering, PMM, content design, brand, and product—facilitating alignment, integrating feedback, and keeping projects moving 

• Partner deeply with engineering throughout the design process, from exploring technical possibilities and constraints early, to co-creating solutions at the intersection of craft and code, and ensuring design intent carries through to final implementation 

• Develop and advance design systems, patterns, and components specific to your surfaces, ensuring they are extensible and maintainable at scale 

• Apply and evolve visual and interaction standards that uphold the quality bar across diverse surface types—from immersive event experiences to conversion-focused product pages • Use research insights, user testing, and performance data to ground your decisions and advocate for the user across partner conversations 

• Actively contribute to team quality, sharing your expertise, setting an example in critique, and helping raise the standard of work across the Presence team 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 5–7 years of relevant design experience, ideally in web, product marketing, or brand contexts 

• A strong portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft, systems thinking, and the ability to lead complex, multi-faceted design work independently 

• Proven ability to own projects end-to-end and deep fluency in layout, typography, color, motion, and interaction 

• Comfort navigating ambiguity: you can generate a clear plan from a loose brief and bring partners along with you 

• Strong communication skills: you articulate your thinking clearly, manage expectations proactively, and reduce confusion rather than add to it 

• Proficiency in Figma, experience working within component-based design systems, and fluency with AI design tools and workflows 

• Experience designing for CMS-driven websites with modular, scalable systems 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience designing event or campaign-driven marketing experiences (conferences, product launches, brand moments) 

• Familiarity with designing for financial products or developer audiences, where clarity and trust are design requirements 

• Fluency with front-end development workflows—you can collaborate meaningfully with engineers on what's possible and what's right 

• Experience designing for international audiences, multilingual surfaces, or accessibility requirements 

• Experience owning or contributing to design across multiple distinct web properties or brand identities simultaneously

 We care deeply about craft—but also about moving with urgency and focus. We seek feedback early and often, because we believe design gets stronger through collaboration and iteration. We keep our users front and center—whether that's a developer evaluating Stripe for the first time, a shopper encountering Link at checkout, or a fintech founder learning about Bridge. And we take pride in shipping work that is not only beautiful and precise, but that delivers clear, measurable impact.

jobs.description:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

 About the team 
 Stripe’s Narrative & Editorial team brings together Content Marketing, Brand Marketing, Portfolio Product Marketing, Copywriting, Copy Editing, and Customer Marketing. We create coherent, distinctive stories about the businesses, technologies, and economic forces shaping the internet.

 What you’ll do 
 We are hiring a senior editorial leader to help bring original stories and insights from Stripe–based on our data, expertise, and customer conversations–to a broader audience via media partnerships and other brand marketing channels. This person will be an exceptional editor, writer, and creative partner with strong instincts about what earns attention: an argument worth making, an unexpected angle, an elegant execution, or a piece of work that people genuinely want to share.

 This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the leader of Stripe’s Narrative & Editorial team. The role will spend most of its time shaping major external media partnerships, with the remainder split between helping with original editorial work and advising partner teams on new ideas and their execution.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Lead the editorial and creative direction for Stripe’s most important external media partnerships, including advertising content, research-led collaborations, and original editorial programs developed with respected publishers and creators. 

• Develop work that feels native to the audience and editorial environment in which it appears—not generic brand messaging placed beside someone else’s work. 

• Turn Stripe’s original data analyses, economic insights, customer stories, and more into content pieces that are clear, surprising, useful, and memorable–and that readers and listeners won’t want to skip over. 

• Shape the full editorial process for partnership work: refining briefs, identifying the strongest ideas, directing creative development, and providing decisive feedback on drafts and final deliverables. 

• Direct and manage agencies, external creators, and editorial partners as needed, working within existing partnership structures and commercial agreements. 

• Write, edit, and materially improve high-stakes content across formats, including blog posts, newsletter segments, podcast scripts, ad copy, social posts, and more. 

• Generate original concepts for creative programs, editorial franchises, and nontraditional formats that broaden how Stripe contributes to conversations about the internet economy. 

• Serve as a trusted thought partner to teams across Stripe, helping them clarify ideas, find the strongest expression of their work, and make better creative decisions. 

• Partner with colleagues in Brand Marketing, Brand Design, Content Marketing, Portfolio PMM, Copywriting, and Customer Marketing to make Stripe’s storytelling more coherent and distinctive. 

• Define and uphold a clear quality bar for editorial and partnership work, making well-reasoned calls about what is ready to represent Stripe and what still needs improvement. 
 
 Who you are 
 We are looking for someone with exceptional editorial judgment and a demonstrated ability to make complicated ideas compelling. You may have developed that experience in a newsroom, independent publication, creative studio, agency, research institution, technology company, or another rigorous creative environment.

 

• You have 8+ years of relevant experience in editorial, writing, creative development, journalism, publishing, media, brand strategy, or a closely related field. This may include experience writing consistently for a large online followership, even if not professionally. 

• You have an exceptional portfolio of published or public-facing work that demonstrates strong writing and editing, original thinking, and an ability to make ideas resonate with an audience. 

• You are, in the best sense, very online: an active reader of and contributor to the newsletters, social platforms, and niche communities where people debate new ideas about technology, economics, science, business, and culture. You can spot emerging arguments, voices, and formats early—and engage with them authentically, with intellectual honesty and your own point of view. 

• You are an excellent editor. You can diagnose what is missing from a draft or idea, identify the most interesting argument, and give feedback that makes the work materially better. 

• You have experience developing original editorial work, sponsored media, advertising, creative partnerships, or other high-quality audience-facing programs. 

• You understand the difference between work that is merely on-message and work that is genuinely interesting, useful, or worth discussing. 

• You can translate complex subjects—including technology, business, economics, science, or policy—into work that is accessible without becoming simplistic. 

• You have strong creative instincts and a sophisticated design sensibility. You understand how language, ideas, visuals, format, and distribution work together. 

• You are deeply curious about the technology industry and the broader cultural and economic context in which it operates. 

• You are comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, external partners, writers, designers, marketers, and agencies without relying on formal authority. 

• You can move fluidly between strategy and execution: developing the core idea, shaping the brief, improving the draft, and making the final call on quality. 

• You have high standards, sound judgment, and enough pragmatism to help teams make excellent work within real constraints.

We build client-side rendering engines, high-performance charting libraries, and interactive visualization interfaces that handle high-throughput streaming telemetry and real-time merchant analytics.

 What you’ll do 
 In this role, you will architect and build high-performance client-side data rendering engines from scratch to visualize tens of thousands of data points smoothly. You will collaborate closely with Designers, Product Managers, and Front-End Systems Engineers to define cutting-edge data visualization paradigms that reduce cognitive load and prevent visual fatigue for Stripe's users.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Partner with designers and product managers to prototype, build, and ship interactive analytics dashboards and data visualization tools across the Stripe Dashboard. 

• Contribute to Stripe’s core design system by developing scalable, reusable visualization components and charting standards for engineering teams. 

• Design frontend integration strategies and robust API contracts to enable seamless adoption of analytics components by partner teams. 

• Provide technical leadership and mentorship through code reviews, pairing, and fostering frontend engineering best practices. 

• Collaborate across Product, Design, Data Infrastructure, and Analytics teams to deliver high-quality, data-driven user experiences. 

• Optimize rendering performance and state management for web applications handling large datasets, real-time telemetry, and high-density visual components. 
 
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 2+ years of relevant web front-end development or creative technology experience in a tech-forward, product-driven company. 

• Advanced experience with React, modern TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML5, CSS/Sass, and modern web application architecture. 

• Demonstrated experience building interactive web charts and visualizations using tools and libraries such as D3.js, Recharts, SVG, Canvas, or WebGL, with a focus on data density and visual-perceptual hierarchy. 

• Proven track record of writing clear, elegant, well-tested code in a collaborative team environment. 

• Deep experience designing and developing web applications that function seamlessly across modern browsers, screen dimensions, and devices. 

• Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively alongside technical and non-technical stakeholders alike. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Passion for crafting beautiful data experiences on the web, demonstrated through a design portfolio or frontend codebase showcasing interactive dashboards, custom charting engines, creative tools, or design systems. 

• Exemplary understanding of formal design principles including typography, layout, color theory, data density balance, and visual proportion beyond basic web UI. 

• Experience building sophisticated interactive tools encompassing complex client-side state management, caching, and real-time data fetching strategies. 

• Advanced proficiency with React, with an emphasis on fluid interactions, subtle animations, visual refinement, and web rendering performance. 

• Experience with accessibility (a11y) standards for interactive charts and graphs, A/B testing frameworks, synthetic monitoring, and performance profiling tools.

 What you’ll do 
 You will build and run a commercial Works in Progress events program, focusing on the US. You will design events that people want to attend and that you can sell and grow sponsorship for. You will identify sponsors and partners, approach and pitch to them, and be responsible for meeting pre-agreed revenue and audience targets.

 We currently offer infrequent events as one of the perks of being a subscriber to the magazine. Our existing community events program includes subscriber events in cities all over the world, particularly San Francisco; New York; Washington, DC; London; Dublin; and Brussels. 

 You will assess where there are opportunities to raise revenue from our existing pipeline of events or by repeating existing formats, identify which events should be retired, and design new formats of events with commercial potential.

 You will have the freedom to design your own events program, which may include a flagship annual summit, salons, themed dinners and lectures. The Works in Progress editorial and operations teams will support you on programming: you will recommend speakers and formats, and we will sign them off. • Exceptional knowledge of fintech industry landscape, trends, and technology 

• Proven expertise in partnering with regional marketing and sales teams to build, grow, and develop pipeline 

• Analytical acumen, with the ability to build, interpret, and adjust measurement tools and data 

• Exceptional presentation, writing, and communication skills, especially to executive stakeholders 

• Appetite and ability to work through ambiguity, evaluate and recommend solutions, and drive clarity across complex, global stakeholder groups 

• Ability to build campaigns and programs from the ground, orchestrating many moving parts across disparate functions

• Experience in the payments, financial technology, or adjacent industries or marketing fintech and/or crypto solutions 

• Integrated campaigns experience focused on select audiences: crypto, enterprise, financial services, fintech companies 

• Product campaigns experience focused on payments, crypto, financial services, and/or embedded finance

jobs.description:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead.  About the team 
 Stripe Terminal helps businesses extend their online presence into the physical world. Our mission is to make it as easy for businesses to accept in-person payments as the Stripe API has made it for online payments. With Terminal, businesses can create flagship retail experiences, extend their websites to pop-up stores, or enable mobile point-of-sale payments at their next event. All of this is built on the Stripe Payments Platform, so businesses can maintain a single view of customers and sales across online and offline channels.

 Our hardware engineering team in Taiwan designs and builds the physical payment devices at the heart of that experience, including products such as the Stripe Reader S700 and Stripe Reader M2. We are expanding the team and seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical and Industrial Design Engineer who can own both the structural engineering and aesthetic form language of our next generation of payment terminals. This is a blended role. You will be equally comfortable driving design for manufacturability (DFM) for a plastic enclosure and sketching form concepts that express Stripe's design identity in hardware.

 What you'll do 
 You will lead the industrial and mechanical design of next-generation Stripe Terminal payment devices, shaping their form, feel, usability, and structural performance from early concepts through mass production. You will partner with cross-functional teams and suppliers to deliver manufacturable, high-quality hardware, including enclosure design, color, material, and finish specifications, packaging, validation, and production readiness.

 Responsibilities 
 Industrial design 
 

• Lead ideation and concept development through rapid hand sketching, digital sketching, and physical foam or 3D-printed models to explore form factors early in the product lifecycle. 

• Define the visual and tactile design language of Terminal hardware, including proportion, form, surface transitions, button feel, and overall product character. 

• Produce photorealistic product renders using KeyShot or similar tools to communicate design intent to cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders. 

• Define and manage color, material, and finish (CMF) specifications. Work directly with suppliers to qualify target surfaces, textures, and coatings. 

• Manage packaging design, working directly with suppliers to qualify final deliverables and the unboxing experience. 

• Apply ergonomics and human factors principles to ensure products are intuitive and comfortable for a diverse range of users and environments. 

• Maintain visual consistency and brand coherence across the Terminal hardware product family, in alignment with Stripe's design identity. 
 
 Mechanical engineering 
 

• Design mechanical components and assemblies using SolidWorks or Creo, following professional engineering standards. 

• Hands on experience in mechanical designs and drawings, assess manufacturability, and resolve technical problems. 

• Lead and plan problem-solving activities using scientific approaches, such as tolerance analysis, computer-aided engineering (CAE) and finite element method (FEM) simulations, design of experiments (DOE), and physical prototyping. 

• Independently analyze and verify mechanical designs, identify risks, and propose mitigations. 

• Manage bill of materials (BOM) cost and design schedules from a mechanical engineering perspective. 

• Prepare mechanical engineering deliverables, including BOMs, component specifications, and support for failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) activities. 

• Review Design fixtures and calibration processes for high-precision mechanical assemblies. 

• Verify and qualify components in first-article builds from suppliers, and participate in pilot production. 

• Produce and maintain engineering documents, including specifications, design-for-excellence (DFx) guidelines, technical reports, and gate-review packages. 

• Partner with Quality and Reliability teams to support successful validation outcomes and improve hardware durability standards. 

• Support product compliance and certification activities, including Payment Card Industry (PCI) and regulatory certifications. 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements listed below. If you meet these requirements, we strongly encourage you to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, or a closely related field. 

• 8+ years of hands-on product design experience spanning mechanical engineering and industrial design, with a portfolio of consumer or commercial hardware products. This includes experience designing consumer-grade plastic enclosures for handheld products, such as smartphones, tablets, or payment terminals, from concept through mass production. 

• Ability to communicate design concepts through hand or digital sketching at the pace of a design conversation, and experience defining CMF specifications with suppliers. 

• Solid understanding of manufacturing and mechanical production processes, with direct experience taking industrial design concepts through DFM, tooling, and production. 

• Proficiency in mechanical CAD software. Creo is required, and SolidWorks is a plus. Expertise in creating detailed 2D drawings and performing geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance analysis. 

• Familiarity with mold design, first-article inspection (FAI) processes, and process capability (Cpk) analysis, along with experience managing supplier and factory relationships. 

• Strong written and spoken English and Mandarin communication skills to collaborate directly with suppliers in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and mainland China throughout product development and production. Willingness to travel internationally, including to Hong Kong and mainland China, as needed. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Proficiency in rendering software, with KeyShot strongly preferred. VRED or Blender experience is also valued. 

• Experience maintaining a coherent design language across a multi-SKU hardware product family or accessory ecosystem. 

• Familiarity with ergonomics methodologies, including grip studies, anthropometric data, and usability evaluations, applied to handheld device design. 

• Experience with point-of-sale hardware, payment terminals, or consumer electronics peripherals. 

• Knowledge of PCI hardware requirements, material properties, and associated manufacturing processes. 

• Proficiency in thermal calculations and an understanding of plastic material properties. 

• Experience with mechanical simulation tools and metal-part design. 

• Ability to create compelling design presentations for cross-functional and executive audiences, clearly articulating the rationale behind design decisions.

About Privy 
 Our mission is to make privacy and user ownership the default online. To do so, we build simple, flexible APIs and tools for developers that make it easy to build new products on crypto rails.

 Privy owns the abstractions and infrastructure layer above wallets, integrating across chains, third-party providers, and Stripe products like Treasury and Link. We get to solve hard technical problems while leveraging Stripe's distribution to reach customers like Ramp, Klarna, Deel, Kraken, Hyperliquid, and Fomo — powering experiences for both mainstream users and crypto natives.

 Learn more about Privy: Privy and Stripe: Bringing crypto to everyone 

 What you’ll do 
 We’re looking for an exceptional social and content marketer to help shape how some of the most important products in crypto show up on the internet.

 This is a hybrid role: part social lead, part writer and editor, part content strategist. You’ll own how Privy, Bridge, and Stripe Crypto show up across social, primarily on X and LinkedIn, while developing content that extends beyond the feed.

 You’ll turn product launches, customer stories, technical concepts, and industry conversations into sharp, compelling content across short- and long-form formats. You’ll work closely with the Head of Marketing and broader marketing team to find the stories worth telling, partnering with Product, Engineering, and other teams to bring them to life.

 This is a high-ownership role for someone with exceptional writing instincts, strong editorial judgment, and a deep understanding of how great technology brands show up online.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Own social across Privy, Bridge, and Stripe Crypto, from editorial planning and drafting through publishing and engagement, primarily across X and LinkedIn. 

• Turn complex products and technical concepts into sharp, accessible stories, partnering across Marketing, Product, and Engineering to understand what we’re building and why it matters. 

• Develop content across short- and long-form formats, from social posts and threads to blog posts, explainers, customer stories, and event coverage. 

• Build and evolve distinct voices across brands and channels, ensuring our content is clear, confident, technically credible, and native to each platform. 

• Stay close to crypto, fintech, and developer communities, identifying conversations, emerging narratives, and cultural moments where we have something meaningful to contribute. 

• Bring a social-first lens to launches and campaigns, helping shape the story, format, and creative approach from the beginning. 

• Experiment with new formats, including short-form video, product demos, graphics, and other platform-native content, creating scrappily or working with creative partners when needed. 

• Surface community insights across Marketing and Product, including what’s resonating, what people are asking, and where conversations are shifting. 

• Use performance and qualitative signals to improve our content strategy, while building scalable systems for editorial planning, publishing, and measurement. 
 
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 4+ years of experience across social, content marketing, editorial, brand, or adjacent roles in technology, fintech, crypto, or other fast-moving industries. 

• An exceptional writer and editor who can move comfortably between a sharp X post, a thoughtful LinkedIn post, and a substantive long-form piece. 

• Strong editorial judgment and taste: you know what makes a story interesting, what belongs on which platform, and when an idea needs a different format entirely. 

• Deep fluency in X and LinkedIn, including how audiences, formats, and conversations differ across platforms. 

• Comfortable going deep on technical concepts and translating them into clear, compelling content without losing accuracy or nuance. 

• Strong instincts for internet-native storytelling and emerging formats. You don’t need to be a professional video editor or designer, but you know what good looks like and can find scrappy ways to bring ideas to life. 

• A strong cross-functional collaborator who asks sharp questions, synthesizes quickly, and can turn incomplete inputs into strong finished work. 

• Analytical and curious: you care about why something worked, not just how many impressions it received, and use those learnings to make the next thing better. 

• Self-directed, collaborative, and adaptable: you thrive in fast-moving environments, navigate ambiguity well, and are comfortable owning work from idea through publication. 
 
 Strong plus 
 

• Experience working in crypto, fintech, developer tools, or another technically complex category. 

• Existing fluency in crypto and stablecoins, and an understanding of the communities and conversations that shape the industry. 

• Experience creating or commissioning short-form video, product demos, motion, or other multimedia content. 

• Experience operating across multiple brands, products, or audiences while maintaining distinct voices and editorial strategies.

 What you’ll do

Your decisions will directly shape the base operating system, package ecosystems, security posture, and bootstrap behavior of Stripe’s fleet.

 Lead active architectural transformations: The team is driving key platform evolutions, including modernizing the OS configuration layer, containerizing workloads, scaling machine image distribution across multi-cloud regions, and streamlining OS upgrades and critical security patching.

You will tackle complex engineering challenges that balance reliability, security, compliance, developer experience, and performance.

 Your judgment prevents fleetwide incidents: Changes to machine images, packages, kernels, bootstrap systems, and host configuration can have broad consequences. You will design validation, canarying, rollout, health-evaluation, and rollback mechanisms that contain blast radius and make foundational infrastructure changes safer.

 Agency to shape technical strategy: As a Staff engineer, you will set technical direction for the team’s systems, author designs that span multiple teams, mentor engineers and be the person engineering managers and engineers rely on for the technical north-star.

• Design systems and practices that make broad infrastructure changes safe and predictable. Establish strong validation, staged rollout, observability, and rollback capabilities. Build guardrails that prevent unhealthy changes from progressing and give operators clear, actionable information when failures occur. 

• Lead incident response for the systems the team owns. Systematically reduce operational toil and make reliability, security, debuggability, and maintainability first-class properties of the platform.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the Role 
 We're seeking a strategic communications professional to join our team and drive messaging for Anthropic’s Safeguards (Trust & Safety) work, with a focus on making these critical topics accessible and meaningful for everyday users. In this role, you'll craft compelling narratives that resonate with media, policymakers, researchers, and the broader public that help differentiate Anthropic’s approach to building responsible AI.

 The ideal candidate is highly skilled and a creative storyteller with strong proactive and reactive muscle. This role will require working with technical teams to distill complex, technical information into engaging campaigns and editorial that resonate broadly. They should be able to move fast, think critically, and work collaboratively with a wide range of teams on complex issues.

 This is a unique opportunity to shape how one of the world's leading AI companies communicates about safety and responsible development of AI systems at a crucial moment in the industry.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Develop and execute communication strategies that explain the work Anthropic’s Safeguards team is doing, with a particular emphasis on helping everyday users understand our safety measures 

• Effectively plan for and manage crisis communications and provide counsel to a wide range of stakeholders on potential issues and risks 

• Own the comms strategy for Anthropic’s product safety work including new model launches, product features alongside harm areas like child safety, well-being, and mental health 

• Lead cross-functional communications projects that align that align safeguards, research, product, policy, and legal teams around shared messaging and campaigns 

• Craft messaging for major company announcements and milestones that resonates with both technical and non-technical audiences 

• Build strong relationships with journalists and relevant influencers. 

• Oversee executive interviews and speaking engagements. 
 
 You May Be a Good Fit If You 
 

• Have 8+ years of experience working in communications, ideally at a high-growth technology company with consumer facing products. 

• Have a strong record of building proactive communications campaigns that resonate with a diverse range of audiences. 

• Excel at translating complex technical language into compelling messaging that connects with everyday users and are a superb written and verbal communicator. 

• Are excellent at media relations and issues management. 

• Have experience working with research teams and enjoy working cross-functionally with a range of technical and non-technical teams. 

• Want to be part of a fast-paced, small, experienced, and impactful team. 

• Are excited to translate insights about AI for broader audiences. 

• Are results-oriented, with a bias toward flexibility and impact. 

• Care about ensuring that transformative AI systems are developed safely. 
 
 Strong Candidates May Also Have 
 

• Experience working in AI, technology policy, trust and safety comms, user safety or research-driven environments 

• Background working with technical teams including researchers, engineers, or product developers 

• Track record of crisis communications or managing sensitive issues in the public eye 

• Experience communicating about emerging technologies or controversial technical topics 

• Understanding of the AI safety, security, or responsible technology ecosystem 
 The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

 For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

 Annual Salary: $265,000 — $295,000 USD Logistics 
 Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

 Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

 Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

 Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

 How we're different 
 We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

 The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

 Come work with us! 
 Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. About Gusto 

 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

 About Design at Gusto 

 Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We're a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don't care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference. We believe great design can make hard things possible, even delightful.

 We are building an AI-native design organization — and we mean that seriously. We're looking for designers who are already working this way: using AI to prototype ideas quickly, shorten customer feedback loops, and ship quality UX directly to customers. This isn't a future aspiration — it's how we work now, and it's changing what the design role looks like at Gusto and across the industry.

 About the Role 

 This is a leadership role, empowering a team of Product Designers. And, as the first Design Leader for Gusto's Banking team, you'll lead design across two products at different stages of maturity: Wallet, a long-running, established product already helping workers manage their pay, and SMB Banking, a newer banking product for small businesses. You're bringing together an established Consumer Banking design practice with a newer Business Banking effort for the first time, building the shared rituals and practices that will connect them, while staying close enough to the craft to help both products grow.

 This is a player-coach role, for now — but as Banking grows, this role's balance of hands-on craft versus people leadership will shift over time.  Gusto is building the financial platform that small businesses will rely on for the next decade, and AI is at the center of that. From how businesses move money, to how Gusto manages risk and verifies identity, AI is changing what's possible across every part of the experience. The design challenge is defining what it looks like to build those products right: not just faster and smarter, but genuinely trustworthy for the hundreds of thousands of businesses and employees who depend on them.

 As the Product Designer, Finance, you'll set the UX vision and strategy across four interconnected product areas: Business Money, Consumer Money, Payments, and Risk. Your role is to see what individual teams can't, identifying opportunities and systemic gaps that span the full financial experience, and to drive the work that makes Gusto's financial products feel clear, trustworthy, and empowering for hundreds of thousands of small businesses and their employees. Nobody has fully figured out what AI-first financial UX looks like at scale. This role is the chance to define it at Gusto. This role's level is similar to Senior Staff. 

 Your work will span the full scope: defining a long-term UX vision that connects financial and trust experiences across teams, identifying and driving high-impact opportunities that no single pod could tackle alone, and shaping product strategy alongside product directors and engineering leaders. You'll step in as a direct IC on the highest-priority projects, develop other designers, and contribute platform patterns that scale beyond the Money and Risk teams.

As Gusto deepens its financial ecosystem, this team sits at the center of making money movement faster, simpler, and more empowering for hundreds of thousands of small businesses and the people who work for them.

 The Risk team is the trust layer that makes all of it possible. They build the systems that protect customers and Gusto from fraud and financial exposure, and the identity infrastructure that determines how customers verify who they are and how they access Gusto's financial products. It's foundational work: quiet when it's working, critical when it's not.

• Set the UX vision and strategy across the Money and Risk teams, connecting the dots across multiple pods and ensuring a cohesive experience throughout the platform. 

• Identify and drive high-impact design opportunities across the Money and Risk teams, spotting what individual pods can't see from inside their area, and bringing the right partners along to pursue them. 

• Influence product strategy, roadmap priorities, and team OKRs across Money and Risk through a design lens—operating as a senior design co-owner alongside product directors and engineering leaders. 

• Define what AI-first financial UX looks like at Gusto, including how to represent uncertainty clearly, surface errors gracefully, preserve user agency when AI recommendations are wrong, and build trust across consequential automated decisions. 

• Own how the Money and Risk teams build and share customer understanding: setting learning priorities, synthesizing insights across pods, and ensuring customer knowledge consistently informs direction rather than sitting siloed within individual teams. 

• Shape and raise the quality bar for experiences across the Money and Risk teams through hands-on design work, setting direction, and ensuring what ships reflect a high standard of craft. Step in as a direct IC on specific projects when necessary. 

• Develop other designers on Money and Risk through coaching, critique, and structured mentorship, acting as a force multiplier, not just a strong individual contributor. 

• Champion and evolve Gusto's design system and platform standards through your product work, contributing patterns and frameworks that scale beyond Money and Risk. 
 
 Here’s what we're looking for: 

 

• 10+ years of Product Design experience, with a track record of leading design direction across multiple teams, pods, or product domains simultaneously, not just a single-product or single-pod context. 

• You've designed for high-trust, high-stakes experiences where errors have real consequences and clarity is non-negotiable (e.g. payments, risk, compliance, healthcare, or similar). Fintech or financial services background is a plus. 

• You've shaped product strategy at the domain or portfolio level alongside product directors and engineering leaders, not just executed within a single product scope. 

• You have a high bar for craft and stay hands-on, prototyping, iterating, and shipping alongside strategy, not just advising from above. You raise the bar for the designers around you through coaching, critique, and mentorship. 

• You advance experience architectures and service models that span multiple teams, identifying systemic opportunities and organizational barriers, and driving changes that improve coherence and outcomes at scale. 

• You thrive in ambiguity, lead through influence across teams, and are skilled at anticipating organizational friction, structuring how design work is coordinated across multiple teams to maximize impact and reduce drag. 

• You actively use AI in your own design practice and can direct others to do the same, evaluating AI-generated outputs critically, knowing when to override or course-correct, and raising the quality bar on AI-assisted work across the teams you support. 

• You have a point of view on how AI is changing product design, and you've acted on it. You can articulate what you've learned and where you think it's going.

 At Gusto, HR Experiences (HRX) helps small businesses get expert HR help right inside the product. Instead of hunting through forms and menus — or Googling what the law requires — a customer can simply say what they need, and Gusto does the rest: taking the action, answering the question, or bringing in a human expert when the stakes are high. 
 
 
 As a Product Designer on HRX, you'll shape these AI-native experiences end to end, in a domain where getting it right builds real trust — and getting it wrong has real consequences for our customers. That's exactly why judgment, taste , and craft matter here in a way they don't in lower-stakes products. 
 
 
 About the Team: 
 
 
 HRX is building the guidance and service layer that turns HR from a source of tension into a source of confidence for small businesses. We design across the full experience — the everyday self-serve moments, the AI that guides and does the work, and the human HR experts who step in when it matters most — so it all feels like one Gusto. 
 
 
 Gusto Design is operating in an AI-native way, and HRX is one of the teams fostering that hardest. We expect designers here to bring AI fluency in two directions: 
 
 

• 
 AI in your workflow. Using AI to explore ideas, prototype, and synthesize research — so you progress faster without losing craft. 
 

• 
 AI in the product. Designing the experience of AI outputs — representing uncertainty, surfacing errors gracefully, preserving user agency when a recommendation conflicts with best practice, and knowing when a human should step in. 
 
 
 Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: 
 

• 
 Shape AI-native HR experiences end to end — where the customer says what they need and the product delivers the right outcome, without exposing the underlying complexity. 
 

• 
 Lead service design across a two-sided experience — journey mapping and blueprinting the routing and handoffs between the customer, the AI, and human HR experts. 
 

• 
 Make and defend judgment calls about AI outputs — when they're ready to ship, when to keep a human in the loop, and when they shouldn't ship at all — designing for failure so trust holds in the hard moments. 
 

• 
 Ground the work in a specific customer and hold a high craft bar from strategy through pixel-level execution. 
 

• 
 Partner with PM, engineering, and data as a co-owner of product direction — framing ambiguous problems early and spearheading clarity when the picture isn't yet clear. 
 

• 
 Work in fast cycles: set a clear target for an experience, ship real things to customers, and let what you learn sharpen the direction. 
 

• 
 Conduct and direct research with customers and HR experts to validate decisions in a high-stakes, compliance-sensitive domain.

 6+ years of product design experience owning and shipping work in a B2B SaaS environment, with robust craft across web.
